answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a time-bonded inlet: new identities start at zero influence and earn it only through continuous, publicly recorded work. Standing glows like a lantern, bright while productive, dimming when idle, so influence must be constantly re-earned. Decision power requires a summit: a random deep audit by established peers demanding fresh, non-copyable proof of that identity's history. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must run a thousand real workers for months and pay full audit costs per identity, making every Sybil as expensive as a genuine participant.
